summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would allow annual charges to be prescribed for similar biological products grouped within one entry in the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods.
A single charge, with its amount set by regulations, would apply to grouped biologicals sharing one biological number rather than separate charges for separate entries.
It would commence with companion medicines legislation that enables biological products to share an entry, and would not commence if that legislation does not proceed.
changes: Grouped biologicals would be removed from the provision governing annual charges for individual biological entries.
A charge would be payable if the grouped entry operated at any point during the relevant financial year.
The new charge provision would apply to financial years starting on or after commencement.
summary.affected: Sponsors of biological products are affected.

speeches.speaker: Rebecca White
speeches.brief: Moved the Therapeutic Goods (Charges) Amendment Bill 2026 for second reading, proposing annual charges for grouped biologicals included in the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods and stating that the measure would support related reforms while reducing industry costs and regulatory burden.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Declared that specified telecommunications, therapeutic goods, biosecurity, and wine legislation would stand referred to the Federation Chamber, either immediately or following adjournment of second-reading debates, unless otherwise ordered.

speeches.speaker: Melissa McIntosh
speeches.brief: Moved a second reading amendment on two Therapeutic Goods bills, supporting earlier notification of medicine discontinuations and streamlined biologic registrations but arguing that more action is needed to address underlying shortages. The amendment called for a comprehensive policy to strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity and reduce shortages; the coalition would not oppose the bill and reserved its position on amendments.

speeches.speaker: Tania Lawrence
speeches.brief: Explained that the Therapeutic Goods Amendment (Medicines Shortages and Other Measures) Bill 2026 would require 12 months' notice of permanent medicine discontinuations, strengthen supply information powers, update the Medicines Watch List and add clinical-trial inspection powers, citing shortages of quetiapine and ADHD medicines and the importance of earlier planning for patients, pharmacists, hospitals and researchers; debate was adjourned.
